details:
MISSIONFORGE is an interactive educational game about planning and operating a space mission. Players choose a destination and configure a spacecraft, science payload, launch vehicle, power system, and trajectory. They then advance through mission events, make operations decisions, and receive a report explaining how their choices affected the mission’s science goals and engineering constraints.

The game uses public NASA and JPL resources, including mission-history information, planetary data, and JPL Horizons Earth–Mars distance snapshots. For Mars, the game uses those distances to estimate light-time. It clearly separates sourced facts from simplified gameplay assumptions: customizable spacecraft performance, journey pacing, and outcome rules are educational models, not flight predictions.

MISSIONFORGE helps learners explore systems engineering by showing how mass, power, budget, communications delay, and reliability interact. Its creative approach combines mission planning, an animated voyage, research briefings, and an explainable mission diagnosis in one experience.

The project was built with React, TypeScript, TanStack Start, and Tailwind CSS, and is hosted on Cloudflare Workers. Lovable, v0, Antigravity/Gemini, and ChatGPT/Codex assisted with coding, interface iteration, and writing; the team reviewed the results. No physical hardware was used.
